name: 本気つけ麺山下 (Honki Tsukemen Yamashita)

claims.text: Both tsukemen use wheat noodles dipped in a wheat-soy-sauce-based tare, so there is no celiac-safe option and gluten is intrinsic to every bowl.
The fish broth is a soy-sauce (shoyu) base, which in Japanese ramen is standard wheat-containing soy sauce.
Fish broth uses bonito and dried sardines; the tantan bowl is topped with meat-miso, so animal products are central to both dips.

name: 鳳舞楼 京都本店 (Houmairou Kyoto Honten)

claims.text: Wheat noodles and a soy-sauce-seasoned chicken/kombu ankake gravy are central to the menu; no gluten-free preparation or separate handling is described by any source.
The savory ankake gravy is built on chicken-and-kombu dashi finished with soy sauce; standard Japanese soy sauce is wheat-brewed, and no wheat-free tamari is mentioned.
Core broth and gravy are chicken-and-kombu based, and signature dishes feature pork and shrimp; no plant-based broth or vegan menu is offered.
Single-item wheat-noodle ramen shop with one small kitchen; wheat noodles are handled throughout, so any dish would face cross-contamination. No gluten-free handling is offered.
The broth is a soy-based (醤油/清湯) chuka-soba; Japanese shoyu used in such tare is virtually always wheat-containing. No wheat-free tare is indicated.
Broth is pork-bone and chicken-carcass based with house-made pork chashu; the kitchen is built entirely around animal products, so no vegan separation exists.
House-made pickles (お漬物) are served with the bowl to refresh the palate, and chashu and menma are made in-house — a sign of a careful, hands-on kitchen, though not an allergen accommodation.

name: 一盌 清右衛門 (Ichiwan Seiemon)

claims.text: Single small counter kitchen serving wheat-noodle ramen; no dedicated gluten-free prep or separate equipment is documented, so wheat cross-contact is effectively unavoidable.
The signature Kyoto soy sauce bowl is seasoned with a blend of two soy sauces from a local maker; Japanese soy sauce normally contains wheat.
Broths and toppings are animal-based (dashi-forward broth, Iga mochi pork chashu; the miso bowl uses rendered beef fat), so no vegan-safe path on the menu.

name: いいちょ ラーメン (Iicho Ramen)

claims.text: The bowl is built on wheat ramen noodles and a wheat soy-sauce (Sawai shoyu) tare, so gluten is central to the dish; no gluten-free preparation is offered.
The tare is Sawai shoyu, a twice-fermented double-koji soy sauce, which is wheat-based.
Broth is chicken-bone and pork-bone based with back fat and chashu; the yakimeshi uses egg and pork fat. No vegan/vegetarian item exists, so all cooking surfaces and stock are animal-based.

name: 今出川まぜそば戦車 (Imadegawa Mazesoba Sensha)

claims.text: The mazesoba is served in a sweet-spicy tare (甘辛いタレ); such tare is standard soy-sauce-based and wheat-containing, though the shop does not publish its ingredients.
Base bowl and signature special contain pork and fish powder, and raw egg is a standard add-on; no vegan preparation is described.

Many menu items are naturally rice-based rather than wheat-noodle — Khao Man Gai (jasmine rice + poached chicken), pho and pad thai (rice noodles), and curries over rice — which can suit a gluten-avoiding diner better than the wheat ramen the street is known for, though sauces should still be checked.
An organic vegetable market on the ground floor supplies the kitchen, and the menu includes plant-forward salads, chilled tofu, and a green curry with a vegetarian option.

name: イワサキタンメン (Iwasaki Tanmen)

claims.text: The core dish uses wheat ramen noodles in a shared salt broth; there is no published gluten-free option and the kitchen is a small single-line operation, so cross-contact with wheat should be assumed.
The shop's tare is described as a house-made salt (shio) sauce rather than a soy-based one; however, its full composition is not published, so wheat content cannot be confirmed.
Vegetables are stir-fried together with pork, and the broth is chicken/pork based, so vegetable toppings share animal ingredients and equipment.
Diners can customize vegetables, pork, noodle amount, garlic and spice level, with garlic served separately for portion control — useful for tailoring a bowl, though not an allergen accommodation.
